newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Kidston says no dividend this year.
newsitem.headline: Kidston says no dividend this year.

text.p: Kidston Gold Mines Ltd chairman Dick Zandee said on Tuesday the company was unable to pay a dividend this year and would not be able to do so until its financial conditions improved significantly.
"The board firmly believes it is necessary to continue the suspension of dividends until the company's financial conditions improve significantly," Zandee told the annual meeting.
Zandee said Kidston had consistently forecast 1996 and 1997 as "lean years".
Kidston had committed itself to developing the Eldridge gold pit, with costly development for the first two years.

However, Zandee said underlying physical demand for gold was expected to continue this year as Asian economies experienced increased disposable income levels and accompanying increases in gold demand.
Managing director John Shaw told shareholders Kidston was continuing to explore for further gold deposits which might be developed into future production.
"The region surrounding Kidston hosts numerous occurrences of anomalous gold over a wide area," Shaw said.
The objective for Kidston was to identify deposits where that gold was concentrated enough to be economically exploitable, Shaw said.
Kidston is 70-percent owned by Placer Pacific Ltd, the Australian unit of Canada's Placer Dome Inc.
